title: Define the Work Origin contract and cross-project delivery plan
scope: Replace the former shared-ID-allocator implementation scope with planning for Outask Work Origin. Document the agreed coordination contract, obtain approval and create Outask implementation tasks one at a time, then prepare the specification for tasks in the separate Outask Server project and save the agreed decisions in existing project documentation. Outask retains local JSON/Git task storage and contains only a lightweight client plus optional server installation/configuration and systemd command wrappers. Outask Server is a separate Linux system component coordinating multiple registered projects; it requires installed Outask and accessible server-side project checkouts, uses Outask operations to inspect them, and retains current coordination state rather than full task content or history. Cover project identity; stable task field outask_origin_uuid; per-project outask_client names derived from hostname with atomically allocated numeric suffixes for independent clones/worktrees; ownership, status/revision checks and explicitly confirmed force; offline work, ID allocation and conflict reconciliation; shared project addresses and local per-project/network-profile overrides; installation/startup checks, systemd and journald; and rebuilding coordination from an agreed Git state on another host without transferring the server database. Rebuilding requires clients to reconfirm ownership and ID allocations while preserving local work. Do not introduce a coordinator-generation field. Without configured coordination, existing task formats, numeric IDs, statuses, lists and command behavior remain unchanged, no coordination fields are added, and no server/network dependency is introduced. This task delivers the agreed plan and task decomposition only; implementation, server installation/deployment, and task creation in another project are excluded.
acceptance: The saved contract matches the owner's agreed Work Origin model: local JSON/Git content, a lightweight Outask client, and a separate Linux multi-project coordinator requiring installed Outask and registered project checkouts. It defines outask_origin_uuid and outask_client, default hostname-plus-suffix assignment, and separate clients for independently owned clones/worktrees.

The contract specifies unchanged behavior without coordination, including task bytes/fields, numeric ID allocation, statuses, lists and outputs, and no server requests or server-installation requirement. Coordination-field enrollment is explicit.

The plan defines online ownership/status checks across all retained task statuses, offline creation/taking/editing/closing, ID blocks and provisional IDs, explicit confirmation of destructive force and renumbering, safe retries/local recovery, and conflict handling without silently discarding work.

The contract covers shared Git configuration, local project/network-profile address overrides, optional server installation, standard systemd lifecycle commands and journald. It defines rebuilding current coordination state from a selected Git snapshot on a new host without a database transfer or coordinator-generation field; old ownership and allocations require reconfirmation.

Approve and persist Outask implementation tasks one at a time. Each has explicit scope, exclusions, immediately observable value, concrete acceptance checks and non-cyclic dependencies. Preserve task-system allocated IDs and record cross-project prerequisites without inventing identifiers.

After all Outask implementation tasks are approved and created, prepare the Outask Server specification for the separate project, referencing actual Outask task IDs and defining independently verifiable server deliverables. Do not create tasks in that project or start implementation under this planning task.

Save current decisions in their owning Outask documentation, keep acceptance/task references in this task, and verify the documents and saved task scopes agree. Validate and commit changed task stores with refreshed service metadata.

values.goal: Keep repository-local JSON tasks usable by developers and agents working independently across PCs, clones and worktrees.
values.value: The owner has one agreed coordination contract and a scoped, dependency-correct delivery backlog instead of the superseded ID-only implementation plan.
values.observable_result: Approved Outask implementation tasks exist with real IDs; maintained contract documentation and the subsequent separate-project Outask Server specification agree on behavior, scope and verification.
values.verification: Inspect the saved contract, approved task records and dependency order against the agreed online/offline, force, multi-project server, recovery and unchanged-local-mode scenarios; validate the task stores.

Choose the smallest deployable service/storage option during technical design. Do not assume a hosting provider or create paid infrastructure from this planning request. Task creation does not start implementation or deployment.

title: Simplify installer completion messages across platforms
scope: Update the packaged Linux, macOS and Windows installer messages and completion behavior. Remove all suggestions to close the window using keyboard shortcuts, including 'If the window stays open, close it with Cmd+W.'. Always display the canonical short command 'outask' in Command; retain the platform-appropriate full executable path with correct quoting in Run immediately for use before a new terminal is opened. End successful installation with 'Installation complete. Open a new terminal to start working.'. Append 'Press any key to finish.' and wait for a key only in launch contexts where the installer window would otherwise close automatically; omit both the prompt and wait when the terminal remains open. Preserve the installed-location line and readable spacing. This task covers completion messages and pause behavior, not update functionality.
acceptance: Successful installation shows 'Installed Outask at <installation path>.', a blank line, 'Command: outask', 'Run immediately: <correctly quoted full executable path> --help', a blank line, and 'Installation complete. Open a new terminal to start working.'.

macOS output uses the actual paths, for example: Installed Outask at /Users/user/Library/Application Support/Outask. followed by Command: outask and Run immediately: '/Users/user/.local/bin/outask' --help, with the agreed blank lines.
No installer message suggests closing the window with Cmd+W or another keyboard shortcut.
'Press any key to finish.' and its key wait are present only for launch contexts where the window otherwise closes automatically. Persistent terminal sessions show neither the prompt nor the wait.

Focused platform installer checks verify final output, short Command, executable-path quoting for paths containing spaces, and pause behavior in automatically closing windows versus persistent terminals; inspect captured successful installation output at the user boundary and run the applicable project gates.
values: Goal: provide usable packaged CLI/MCP installation on supported Linux, macOS and Windows platforms (docs/product.md). Value: users immediately see the short CLI command and a usable immediate-run command, without unnecessary window-closing instructions or key waits. Observable result: the completed installer presents the agreed concise message and pauses only when needed to keep an automatically closing window readable. Verification: inspect successful installer output and exit/pause behavior for automatically closing launches and persistent terminal sessions on the supported platform routes.

Verify uninstall succeeds when optional configuration or cache paths are absent and that existing protection against removing an unrelated command remains effective.

title: Coordinate online task operations through Work Origin
scope: Implement the lightweight online Work Origin client in shared core/standalone creation and mutation operations and expose aligned behavior through CLI and MCP. Explicit project enrollment assigns stable outask_origin_uuid task identities while retaining numeric IDs, existing records and unknown fields. Register each independent clone/worktree as outask_client using hostname plus a server-assigned numeric suffix; reconnecting the same copy preserves its identity, while independent copies and coincident hostnames must not share authority accidentally. Coordinate creation, taking ownership, changes, completion and archival across every retained status/store, checking current ownership and revisions. Reject unintended edits to another client's work and stale changes; require explicit confirmation tied to the concrete operation and expected state for force, including destructive replacement of an occupied ID. Recover safely from lost replies and local write failures without duplicate tasks or repeat application. Keep server traffic limited to coordination data; local JSON/Git retain full task content. Preserve unchanged non-coordinated task formats, numeric allocation, statuses, lists, outputs and network-free operation. Update affected user/contributor contracts and pass required checks. Offline reconciliation, server implementation/installation/systemd management and Git-hook integration are excluded and belong to subsequent delivery tasks.
acceptance: Against a real Outask Server, two independent project directories concurrently create tasks with distinct positive safe-integer numeric IDs and outask_origin_uuid values; project identity isolates unrelated projects and all retained IDs remain occupied.

Independent clones/worktrees register distinct outask_client identifiers with atomically allocated hostname-based suffixes. Reconnection retains the same client; hostnames alone do not grant another client's authority. Coordination enrollment is explicit and preserves existing task fields and records.

Two clients attempting to take the same task concurrently yield one successful owner and a clear conflict for the other. Ordinary edits, completion, archival and other mutations reject conflicting ownership or stale state across all retained statuses, including custom statuses.

CLI and MCP force flows require explicit confirmation of a concrete operation, affected task, owner, expected state and destructive consequences. Changed state invalidates prior confirmation; no permanent blanket force permission is introduced. An occupied numeric ID can be explicitly replaced, never duplicated within the final store.

Lost replies and retries do not create an additional task or apply an operation twice. Exercise local failure after server authorization and recovery without silently overwriting another client's work. Network waits do not hold the local writer lock; ordinary validation and local write coordination still apply.

Without configured Work Origin, regression checks demonstrate unchanged task fields/bytes, numeric ID allocation, statuses, lists and command outputs, with no coordination requests, added fields or installed-server dependency.

Exercise actual shared operations, standalone/CLI and MCP boundaries against the runnable server using two independent directories. Document enrollment, online conflicts, confirmation and recovery; keep public help/contracts aligned and pass required CI. Fixtures alone do not satisfy real-server acceptance.

values.value: Connected participants obtain unique task numbers and protection against accidentally taking or changing another client's work.
values.observable_result: Two real Outask clients connected to one coordinator create distinct tasks, resolve concurrent ownership attempts deterministically and perform intentional overrides only after explicit confirmation.
values.verification: Run concurrent creation and ownership/edit/close/archive scenarios through CLI and MCP against the real server, test lost-reply/local-failure recovery, and verify unchanged server-free operation.

notes: Approved by the owner during task-by-task Work Origin planning under task 9; creation authorizes backlog recording, not implementation.

External prerequisite: the separately owned Outask Server online coordination contract and runnable implementation must be delivered before this task starts. Link its actual project/task reference when that project creates it; no external identifier is reserved or invented. Server delivery must not depend on this client's completion and must be independently verifiable.

The owner requires offline-capable coordinated work in the completed feature. The online slice does not settle offline behavior; a subsequent approved task owns offline continuation and reconciliation.
